frontmatter.title: Peak Current and Passives for the 120V to 12V Buck

children.value: Created with Grok Build
This is the wxMaxima 13.04.2 worksheet linked from the
120 V to 12 V buck

, evaluated in Python. The input in the sheet is 130 V, the maximum in the requirements, and the output is 12 V. Each code cell is the worksheet expression. The printed line is that expression’s value.
Peak current resistor selection
I_peak
is 0.1 A.
R_iset
is that current times 10^6, in ohms. The input is 130 V and the output is 12 V.
The note says the frequency will be optimized iteratively, starting from a 100 kHz estimate. The cell that is saved sets the frequency to 200 kHz.
L = \frac{V_{out}}{f \, I_{peak}} \left(1 - \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}}\right)
children.html: L=Voutf Ipeak(1−VoutVin)L = \frac{V_{out}}{f \, I_{peak}} \left(1 - \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}}\right)L=fIpeak​Vout​​(1−Vin​Vout​​)

children.value: The minimum on time is taken from page 11 of the datasheet as 150 ns. Two checks ask whether the inductance is above the minimum. The inductor actually selected is 500 µH.

import math

def show(label, value, unit):
    print(f"{label:<18} {value:.6g} {unit}")

I_peak = 0.1
R_iset = I_peak * 10**6
V_in = 130
V_out = 12
freq = 200_000
L = (V_out / (freq * I_peak)) * (1 - V_out / V_in)
t_on_min = 150e-9
L_test1 = ((V_in * t_on_min) / I_peak) * 1.2
L_test2 = ((V_out * 3.5e-6) / 1) * 1.2
L_actual = 500e-6

show("I_peak", I_peak, "A")
show("R_iset", R_iset / 1e3, "kohm")
show("V_in", V_in, "V")
show("V_out", V_out, "V")
show("freq", freq, "Hz")
show("L", L * 1e6, "µH")
show("t_on_min", t_on_min * 1e9, "ns")
show("L_test1", L_test1 * 1e6, "µH")
show("L_test2", L_test2 * 1e6, "µH")
show("L_actual", L_actual * 1e6, "µH")

children.value: Input and output capacitors
The allowable input ripple is 25 mV. The source is taken to be stiff. The minimum input capacitance is
C_{in} = \frac{L \, I_{peak}^{2}}{2 \, V_{in} \, \Delta V_{in}}
children.html: Cin=L Ipeak22 Vin ΔVinC_{in} = \frac{L \, I_{peak}^{2}}{2 \, V_{in} \, \Delta V_{in}}Cin​=2Vin​ΔVin​LIpeak2​​

children.value: A 1 µF ceramic is used, for the margin and for low ESR. The RMS ripple current in that capacitor is
I_{RMS,in} = I_{peak} \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}} \sqrt{\frac{V_{in}}{V_{out}} - 1}
children.html: IRMS,in=IpeakVoutVinVinVout−1I_{RMS,in} = I_{peak} \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}} \sqrt{\frac{V_{in}}{V_{out}} - 1}IRMS,in​=Ipeak​Vin​Vout​​Vout​Vin​​−1​

children.value: The acceptable output ripple is 50 mV. The sheet’s minimum output capacitance is
C_{out,min} = 100 \, \frac{L_{actual}}{2} \left(\frac{I_{peak}}{V_{out}}\right)^{2}
children.html: Cout,min=100 Lactual2(IpeakVout)2C_{out,min} = 100 \, \frac{L_{actual}}{2} \left(\frac{I_{peak}}{V_{out}}\right)^{2}Cout,min​=1002Lactual​​(Vout​Ipeak​​)2

children.value: The worst-case output-capacitor ripple current is half of
I_peak
. With an ESR of 0.3 ohm, the dissipation is the square of that current times the ESR.

delta_V_in = 25e-3
Cin = (L * I_peak**2) / (2 * V_in * delta_V_in)
C_in_actual = 1e-6
I_RMS_in = I_peak * (V_out / V_in) * math.sqrt((V_in / V_out) - 1)
delta_V_out = 50e-3
C_out_min = ((L_actual / 2) * (I_peak / V_out) ** 2) * 100
I_out_ripple_WC = I_peak / 2
ESR_C_out = 0.3
P_diss_C_out = I_out_ripple_WC**2 * ESR_C_out

show("delta_V_in", delta_V_in * 1e3, "mV")
show("Cin", Cin * 1e6, "µF")
show("C_in_actual", C_in_actual * 1e6, "µF")
show("I_RMS_in", I_RMS_in * 1e3, "mA")
show("delta_V_out", delta_V_out * 1e3, "mV")
show("C_out_min", C_out_min * 1e6, "µF")
show("I_out_ripple_WC", I_out_ripple_WC * 1e3, "mA")
show("ESR_C_out", ESR_C_out, "ohm")
show("P_diss_C_out", P_diss_C_out * 1e3, "mW")

children.value: Input filter
The snubber capacitance is four times the 1 µF input capacitor. The input-filter inductor is picked at 100 µH, to be refined later. The snubber resistor is
R_{snubber} = \sqrt{\frac{L_{filter}}{C_{snubber}}}
children.html: Rsnubber=LfilterCsnubberR_{snubber} = \sqrt{\frac{L_{filter}}{C_{snubber}}}Rsnubber​=Csnubber​Lfilter​​​

children.value:
C_in_snubber = 4 * C_in_actual
L_in_filter = 100e-6
R_snubber = math.sqrt(L_in_filter / C_in_snubber)

show("C_in_snubber", C_in_snubber * 1e6, "µF")
show("L_in_filter", L_in_filter * 1e6, "µH")
show("R_snubber", R_snubber, "ohm")

jupyter_data.name: stdout
jupyter_data.text:

L_in_filter        100 µH
R_snubber          5 ohm

children.value: Feedback divider
The first trial fixes the lower resistor at 100 kohm and solves
V_{out} = 0.8 \left(1 + \frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)
children.html: Vout=0.8(1+R1R2)V_{out} = 0.8 \left(1 + \frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)Vout​=0.8(1+R2​R1​​)

children.value: for the upper resistor. That upper resistor is 1.4 Mohm. The sheet calls it impractical, because the circuit is less stable at low load current with it.
The sheet then sets the voltage the IC regulates to 5 V and divides the 12 V output down to 5 V, using Figure 8 on page 14, with the lower resistor at 10 kohm. The divider equation in the sheet is
V_b = V_a \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}
children.html: Vb=VaR2R1+R2V_b = V_a \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}Vb​=Va​R1​+R2​R2​​

children.value: which solves to
R_1 = R_2 (V_a - V_b) / V_b
children.html: R1=R2(Va−Vb)/VbR_1 = R_2 (V_a - V_b) / V_bR1​=R2​(Va​−Vb​)/Vb​

children.value: . The numeric cell that follows is entered as
-(V_midpoint - V_out * R2_fb) / V_midpoint
, with the midpoint defined as 5 V.

R2_fb_trial = 100e3
R1_fb_trial = R2_fb_trial * (V_out / 0.8 - 1)

R2_fb = 10e3
# Closed form of solve(Vb = Va * R2 / (R1 + R2), R1).
# Va is the 12 V output and Vb is the 5 V midpoint.
R1_from_divider = R2_fb * (V_out - 5) / 5

V_midpoint = 5
R1_fb = -(V_midpoint - V_out * R2_fb) / V_midpoint

show("R2 trial", R2_fb_trial / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R1 trial", R1_fb_trial / 1e6, "Mohm")
show("R2", R2_fb / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R1 from divider", R1_from_divider / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R1 as entered", R1_fb / 1e3, "kohm")

children.value: Undervoltage and overvoltage lockout
The lockout string is 2 Mohm total. The overvoltage threshold is 135 V and the undervoltage threshold is 115 V. R5, R4, and R3 follow Figure 10 on page 15 of the datasheet:

R_5 = R_{total} \frac{1.21}{V_{OVLO}}, \quad
R_4 = R_{total} \frac{1.21}{V_{UVLO}} - R_5, \quad
R_3 = R_{total} - R_5 - R_4
children.html: R5=Rtotal1.21VOVLO,R4=Rtotal1.21VUVLO−R5,R3=Rtotal−R5−R4R_5 = R_{total} \frac{1.21}{V_{OVLO}}, \quad R_4 = R_{total} \frac{1.21}{V_{UVLO}} - R_5, \quad R_3 = R_{total} - R_5 - R_4R5​=Rtotal​VOVLO​1.21​,R4​=Rtotal​VUVLO​1.21​−R5​,R3​=Rtotal​−R5​−R4​

children.value: The values actually used are 18 kohm, 3.16 kohm, and 1.98 Mohm. The sheet then solves those resistors back to the two thresholds. Page 15 requires the OVLO pin to stay under 6 V. The pin voltage is the 130 V input times R5 over the actual string.

R_lockout_total = 2e6
OVLO_threshold = 135
UVLO_threshold = 115
R5 = R_lockout_total * (1.21 / OVLO_threshold)
R4 = (R_lockout_total * (1.21 / UVLO_threshold)) - R5
R3 = R_lockout_total - R5 - R4

R5_actual = 18e3
R4_actual = 3.16e3
R3_actual = 1.98e6
R_total_actual = R5_actual + R4_actual + R3_actual
OVLO_actual = (121 * R_total_actual) / (100 * R5_actual)
UVLO_actual = (121 * R_total_actual) / (100 * R5_actual + 100 * R4_actual)
V_ovlo_pin = V_in * (R5_actual / R_total_actual)

show("R5 calculated", R5 / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R4 calculated", R4 / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R3 calculated", R3 / 1e6, "Mohm")
show("R5 actual", R5_actual / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R4 actual", R4_actual / 1e3, "kohm")
show("R3 actual", R3_actual / 1e6, "Mohm")
show("R total actual", R_total_actual / 1e6, "Mohm")
show("OVLO actual", OVLO_actual, "V")
show("UVLO actual", UVLO_actual, "V")
show("OVLO pin", V_ovlo_pin, "V")

children.value: Soft-start capacitor
The desired soft-start delay is 100 ms. The capacitor is

children.html: CSS=tSS 5×10−60.8C_{SS} = t_{SS} \, \frac{5 \times 10^{-6}}{0.8}CSS​=tSS​0.85×10−6​

children.value: The standard value chosen is 680 nF. The soft-start time with that capacitor is

children.html: tSS=CSS 0.85×10−6t_{SS} = \frac{C_{SS} \, 0.8}{5 \times 10^{-6}}tSS​=5×10−6CSS​0.8​

children.value:
SS_time = 100e-3
C_SS = SS_time * ((5e-6) / 0.8)
C_SS_actual = 680e-9
SS_time_actual = (C_SS_actual * 0.8) / (5e-6)

show("SS_time desired", SS_time * 1e3, "ms")
show("C_SS", C_SS * 1e9, "nF")
show("C_SS actual", C_SS_actual * 1e9, "nF")
show("SS_time actual", SS_time_actual * 1e3, "ms")

children.value: Parts taken from the sheet

The cells above select 500 µH for the power inductor, 1 µF for the input capacitor, 100 µH for the input filter, 5 ohm for the snubber resistor, 18 kohm / 3.16 kohm / 1.98 Mohm for the lockout string, and 680 nF for soft start.
